blocks.content: Quiz: What happens when two rules have the same specificity in CSS?
Tap an option below to answer:
Only one rule can apply to an element. If two rules target the same property, the latest one takes precedence.
Only one rule can apply to an element. If two rules target the same property, the latest one takes precedence.
The rule that is written first in the CSS file is applied.
The rule that comes later in the CSS file is applied when two rules have the same specificity.
The rule that comes later in the CSS file is applied when two rules have the same specificity.
The rule that comes later in the CSS file is applied.
CSS follows a last-rule-wins approach. When several conflicting rules could apply to the same element, the one that comes last in the source code is applied.
CSS follows a last-rule-wins approach. When several conflicting rules could apply to the same element, the one that comes last in the source code is applied.
An external rule being applied depends solely on its specificity, not on its external nature.
An external rule being applied depends solely on its specificity, not on its external nature.
